questions: Does any existing work already combine a document retriever's semantic score with a temporal relevance term based on elapsed time to version timestamps (as opposed to hard version validity filtering or knowledge-graph time scoping)?
Is elapsed time to a version timestamp a valid proxy for legal in-force status, or is the necessary signal validity intervals / effective dates?
Do existing time-sensitive temporal QA benchmarks (TIQ, statutory-QA benchmarks) already contain overlapping document revisions and time-stamped queries, or must a new benchmark be built?
Under what query-date regimes does a soft temporal term help versus induce harmful recency bias?
What is the strongest fair baseline: semantic-only retrieval, hard version filtering, or a recency-boosted retriever?
search_topics: temporal RAG and temporally-aware retrieval-augmented language models
temporal information retrieval and time-sensitive query ranking
legal/statutory question answering with amendments and versions
temporal validity / effective-date filtering in legal retrieval
temporal QA benchmarks with implicit time constraints
recency bias in retrieval and LLM question answering
document version retrieval and superseded legislation
comparison_targets: Semantic-similarity-only retrieval (BM25 and dense bi-encoder) on the same corpus
Hard temporal validity filtering / version filtering RAG (as in Prior et al. 2026, arxiv:2605.23497)
TempRALM temporally-aware RALM with few-shot extensions (arxiv:2401.13222)
